observers.label: Caption-blind observer 1 (Claude)

answers.1: A human head and upper neck, seen from the right side in profile, slightly from behind; the face points right and only the eyelashes, brow, and tip of the nose are visible. Hair is short on top and buzzed on the sides.
answers.2: Two dark-grey objects joined by a thin cable. A round disc sits flat on the buzzed scalp behind and above the ear. A rectangular, oblong unit with a curved hook sits on top of the outer ear, its hook draped over the top of the ear and its body resting behind the ear; a short cable arcs from the disc down into the top of that unit. The skin looks intact, with no redness, swelling, cut, or scar drawn.
answers.3: No text, arrows, labels, or symbols.
answers.4: It could be mistaken for a hearing aid with a magnetic headphone or headset pad, or for a patch stuck to the scalp; a worried patient might read the round disc as something implanted or protruding through the skin.

observers.label: Caption-blind observer 2 (Claude)

answers.1: The back and side of a person's head, neck, and one ear, seen from behind and slightly to the side (a rear three-quarter view). The face is turned away; only the tip of the nose, eyelashes, and eyebrow show at the right edge. The hair is short on top and closely shaved on the sides and back.
answers.2: Two connected dark-gray objects. A round, flat disc with a raised center sits on the shaved scalp above and behind the ear. A thin dark cable runs from the disc down and forward to a curved, oblong unit that hooks over the top of the ear and rests behind it. The oblong unit has a small clear hook over the ear and a tiny red dot near its top. The skin shows no cuts, redness, swelling, or scars.
answers.3: No text, arrows, labels, or symbols.
answers.4: A worried patient might read the disc as something surgically attached to or protruding from the skull, or the whole device as a large hearing aid with a wired clip.
